note: The closed tag vocabulary (spec: kb.data.tags): a page may carry in `tags` only an id listed here. Each term sits in one facet: a `topic` says what the page is about, and an ordinary page carries exactly one, written first, which is the key its hub groups it under, beneath the topic's `label`; a `skill` says what the reader does; a `language` names the machinery. A page writes its tags in facet order, 2 to 5 of them. The tags gate (tools/src/gates/check-tags.ts) holds every page under docs/ and the flat TAGS tuple in site/src/lib/types.ts to this file, both ways; tools/src/gen/gen-taxonomy.ts renders docs/reference/tags.md from it (make taxonomy, or make gen). It is edited by hand, and a term no page uses is a finding, so add one only together with the page that earns it, and its id to the tuple in the same change.

facets.topic: What is the page about? Exactly one per page, written first, and the only facet that groups hub entries.
facets.skill: What quality or design move does the reader practise on the page?
facets.language: What machinery does the page name?

terms.label: Anti-patterns
terms.definition: A named design people adopt on purpose that looks like a solution and makes every later change harder.

terms.label: API design
terms.definition: The shape of a contract between a caller and a service.

terms.label: Caching
terms.definition: Keeping a copy closer or cheaper to read, and paying the staleness bill.

terms.label: Concurrency
terms.definition: More than one thing in flight, and the coordination that demands.

terms.label: Consistency
terms.definition: Which readers see which writes, and when.

terms.label: Coordination
terms.definition: Getting independent participants to agree on something.

terms.label: Data modeling
terms.definition: Choosing the shapes data is stored and queried in.

terms.label: Domain modeling
terms.definition: Letting the business domain, not the database, shape the code.

terms.label: Event-driven design
terms.definition: Reacting to things that happened rather than being told what to do.

terms.label: Integration
terms.definition: Joining systems that were not designed together.

terms.label: Low-level design
terms.definition: Code-level design inside one component: which types and functions exist, what each owns and how they work together.

terms.label: Machine learning
terms.definition: Serving or training models as a systems problem.

terms.label: Messaging
terms.definition: Passing work as messages instead of calls.

terms.label: Modularity
terms.definition: Splitting a system into parts that can be understood alone.

terms.label: Observability
terms.definition: Being able to tell what the system is doing from outside it.

terms.label: Operations
terms.definition: Running the thing: deploys, capacity, incidents.

terms.label: Partitioning
terms.definition: Splitting data or work so no single node holds all of it.

terms.label: Performance
terms.definition: Doing the same work with less time or less hardware.

terms.label: Persistence
terms.definition: Storing state so it outlives the process.

terms.label: Replication
terms.definition: Keeping more than one copy, and reconciling them.

terms.label: Resilience
terms.definition: Degrading rather than collapsing when a dependency fails.

terms.label: Routing
terms.definition: Choosing where a request goes.

terms.label: Scalability
terms.definition: Handling more load by adding capacity rather than rewriting.

terms.label: Security
terms.definition: Keeping a hostile caller from getting what they want.

terms.label: Testing
terms.definition: How the system is proved to work.

terms.label: Transactions
terms.definition: Grouping changes so they land together or not at all.

terms.label: UI architecture
terms.definition: Structuring a client: rendering, state and data fetching.
